name: Datum Mesh
tagline: Finite-element analysis on the desktop: stresses, deflections and temperatures in parts and frames.
for: Mechanical, structural, process and aerospace engineers, students and lecturers.
about: Datum Mesh finds the stresses, deflections and temperatures in parts and structures by the finite-element method. You draw a frame of beams and truss bars, or the outline of a part with its holes, put on the supports and loads, and solve.

Frames and trusses solve now: the deflected shape, the moment, shear and axial diagrams, the reactions, member stresses and utilisation, and an equilibrium check after every solve. Parts are drawn and loaded today; their meshing and solving arrive in 0.1.2, heat conduction and the materials library in 0.1.3. Help › Verification solves benchmarks with known answers in front of you, so you can see how far to trust each result.

steps.title: Draw and mesh
steps.text: Draw a frame of beams and truss bars, or the outline of a part with its holes, on a grid with snap and rulers.

steps.title: Load and support
steps.text: Put supports, forces, pressures, gravity and heat on nodes, members and edges, and set their values with units.

steps.title: Solve and report
steps.text: Solve, read the deflections, stresses and temperatures, and print a report with the equilibrium check.

highlights: Frames and trusses: draw members on a grid, press Solve, and see the deflected shape, moment, shear and axial diagrams and the reactions
An equilibrium check after every solve: the reactions are added up against the loads
Help › Verification: benchmarks with known answers solved in front of you; all agree to better than one part in a billion
Hover a member to read the axial force, shear, moment and deflection at that point; utilisation colours against the yield strength
Sections: rectangle, round bar, tube, box, I, channel, angle, or your own values, with their properties worked out
Parts: rectangles, circles and polygons with arcs, and holes cut out of them, with supports and loads on their edges
SI or US units shown everywhere; files keep SI, so switching never rounds anything
Six worked examples: a portal frame, a roof truss, a lifting lug, an L-bracket with a fillet, a flange plate and a heat sink
